steps.content: NOT for the Faint-Hearted! Chilling Truth Unveiled: Ghost Sightings in Demolition-Bound Complex
"IT" LINGERS! Disturbing Incidents Plague Urban Renewal Project: Midnight Curse Reported
DEMOLITION HALTED BY SUPERNATURAL FORCE? Horrifying CCTV Footage Emerges—And Experts' Shocking Response...

steps.speaker: Real Estate Developer
steps.content: Absolutely not true! Never heard of anything like that!

steps.speaker: Real Estate Developer
steps.content: Is the Bureau seriously blocking our deal with Miss Luminita just because of some baseless tabloid stories?

steps.speaker: Real Estate Developer
steps.content: I understand that you have your concerns, but let's not forget this renewal project is a top priority approved by the government. We can't afford any delays.

steps.speaker: Real Estate Developer
steps.content: The rumors about the haunted old neighborhoods are really hurting our project's reputation. As per our signed agreement, Miss Luminita is obligated to use her expertise as a haunted property inspector to address these rumors.

steps.speaker: Real Estate Developer
steps.content: I've mentioned this multiple times in our previous calls. I strongly urge the Bureau to expedite Miss Luminita's leave permit. Let's put an end to these unnecessary obstacles and time-wasting!
Beep—Beep—

After finishing her report, Nightingale places the documents from the developer on your desk one by one. Alongside the property inspection agreement, the developer has included a structural hazard assessment report for the old neighborhoods.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief, I've verified the report's contents. While I suspect some deliberate exaggeration in the wording, the district has indeed experienced several accidents due to deteriorating infrastructure and does present significant safety hazards.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: During our previous communications, the demolition contractor was evasive when we pressed for details. But judging by the contents of this structural hazard assessment alone, their attitude could be seen as... honest.
Whether it's honesty or pressure tactics, only they know for sure. If they really cared about resident safety, they wouldn't have waited until now to send us this report.
Any updates on the investigation into those haunting rumors in the old district?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Apart from several residents claiming to have witnessed supernatural events, we haven't come across any solid leads. We're still tracking down the source of these rumors.
You give her a nod. Tracking down the source of rumors is always challenging, and the current situation still lies within your expectations.
Fortunately, you have another person directly involved in this matter right here.
You push aside the documents on your desk and pull out Luminita's profile that you were reviewing earlier. Picking up on your intention, Nightingale continues speaking.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: As you requested, we've been conducting a parallel investigation into Sinner Luminita. Every single "haunted property" she's handled as a real estate agent has tested positive for abnormal Mania residue, without exception.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Due to the large number of properties involved and the complexity of the transactions, a more detailed investigation will take additional time. Allowing Luminita to leave the Bureau before the results are complete would indeed pose unnecessary risks.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Regarding the real estate developer's request, should I continue to refuse it on your behalf?
No need. The fact that they can keep contacting us shows they've got some powerful supporters backing them up.
But you're not about to let anyone pull your strings. You want to hear how the Bureau's resident "expert" in haunted property deals explains these ghost-infested old houses.
Nightingale, please move up Luminita's interrogation schedule. I need to speak with her in person before meeting with the real estate developer.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Well hello there, Chief! Finally remembered I exist? You locked me up here and then not a peep from you—I was beginning to think I'd been left in the dust!
As you enter, Luminita, seated in the interrogation chair, brightens up. She eagerly greets you before you can say anything, her words light and cheerful.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: So? You've come to see me today—does this mean you've finally made up your mind about "that thing"?

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Buying a house, of course! What else could it be?

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Remember what I told you just two weeks back? These drops are just normal market fluctuations, and prices will definitely bounce back in six months. Those properties I mentioned last time are all hot listings! Whoever hesitates is lost, Chief. You gotta act fast!

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Of course, buying property is a big decision that deserves careful consideration. But with me on your side, you don't need to worry about prices at all! If the budget is a bit snug, I can find you something even cheaper. I remember there's one at... the crematory out east...
I appreciate you helping me keep an eye out for properties, but I'm afraid that's not why I'm here today.

steps.speaker: test
steps.content: "Yingying"

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: I'm just your friendly neighborhood agent here! No hard sell, no nonsense, just me nudging you because I've got your back. Owning a home equals peace of mind, Chief. As dedicated as you are to work, sleeping at the office isn't the dream, right?
Luminita mutters and grumbles with a show of complaint, but there's no actual trace of displeasure in her voice. She has clearly anticipated your refusal all along.
You observe her reaction and decide to play along with her conversation, gradually steering toward your actual intention.
If we're talking about dedication to work, I can't hold a candle to you. I bet there are fewer than ten people in the entire Bureau who don't have your business card in their pocket.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Just a force of habit... I swear, I wasn't being pushy at all. They practically grabbed my cards themselves!
I understand. I just didn't expect you'd refuse to give yourself a break even while at the Bureau. Is the real estate market that rough out there these days?

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Not really. My business usually does quite well. In real estate, it's all about experience and connections, you know.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: I'm sure you've done some digging into my past. Grew up poor and lied about my age to get jobs, so I started in this business early and do have some connections. Even though I work solo in this gig, it's not really hard for me.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: But...
Luminita taps her cheek with her fingertips, looking noticeably disinterested.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Ever since I landed here, selling houses has been one tough nut to crack!

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Folks around here probably grab my cards just to be nice. Everyone follows your example, Chief—they're all such workaholics they might as well start moving their beds into the office!

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: I can't develop new clients, and I'm not allowed to contact anyone outside. You know, I still had a pile of deals to be closed when I was brought in here.
You avert your gaze, pretending not to notice Luminita's teasing remarks, and continue with your questions.
Seems like agents face the same problems regardless... I thought things might be different for someone specializing in haunted properties like you.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Business is business—the fundamentals never change, and everyone's racing against time. It's just that with haunted houses, profits and trends come and go much faster. Gotta hustle extra hard to keep those earnings flowing since this gig puts food on my table.
If it's such a grind, why did you specifically choose to go into the haunted house business?

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Oh, it's all pretty much the same. Every line of work is tough.
She waves her hand nonchalantly, using an exaggerated sigh to brush off your question. Given Luminita's social acumen, she must have picked up what you were really asking.
Let me cut to the chase. Haunted houses are considered taboo and notoriously difficult to sell. Don't most agents steer clear of these properties?

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Ohh, so that's what you're asking about...
Luminita puts on an expression of sudden comprehension, adjusting her posture. As she moves, the keys beneath her trench coat make a crisp clinking sound—almost like smug laughter.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: That's exactly why they're just your average agents!

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: The haunted house business has its risks, sure, but there's a lot more money to be made.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: I'm not just raking in cash from sales, but also from all those thrill-seekers over in Eastside who flock here for a good scare. Believe it or not, sometimes just selling tickets because of a house's haunted reputation brings in a small fortune!

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Oh, and if you're interested in seeing for yourself...
As she speaks, she pats her pocket. With a quick flick of her wrist, a pristine business card materializes between her fingers, which she promptly thrusts before your eyes.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Once I'm out of the Bureau, hit me up anytime—whether you're house hunting or just curious about haunted spots. Bring your friends, and I'll hook you up with a nice discount!

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Sure, finding real haunted houses is like striking gold these days. But if you're up for a spooky encounter, just swing by my way. I'll make sure you meet a ghost or two!

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: And I'll bump your deal to the top of the list, just for you! You can count on it!

options: There's no rush for my personal deal.

choices.text: There's no rush for my personal deal.

steps.content: You take the business card but don't pocket it, simply placing it next to the documents on the table. Then, you slide the real estate developer's property inspection agreement toward Luminita.
It's too soon to talk about you leaving the Bureau, and my personal deal can wait. Right now, we've got a major case on our hands—and they're asking for your involvement specifically.
There have been some rumors about the old district marked for the government's urban renewal project, and the real estate developer in charge of the project...

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: They're in charge of demolishing the old district, and now they want me to hold up my end of the deal—by proving the area isn't haunted and those houses aren't cursed. Right?

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: I remember it. This is a real estate developer with some bigshot backer we're talking about, after all. And they're generous—just the initial deposit is nearly half a year's income for me.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: No wonder you moved up my interrogation. It's because of this situation, right?
With a theatrical flair, Luminita flips through the agreement with a rustling flourish, not bothering to read any of its contents, before casually tossing the document aside.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: When old buildings seem haunted, it's usually just aging infrastructure or some malfunction. These situations are super easy to fix!

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: With my touch, haunted hellholes turn into dream homes overnight. Only catch? I don't do remote work yet—I'll need to be there in person.
From how you're describing it, were all those "haunted houses" you've handled just cases like this?

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Hmm... Pretty much.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: It's not like ghosts are that common anyway! Living people without homes carry WAY more resentment than any ghost ever could.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: But anyway, Chief, when do you plan to let me out to handle it? It's a major urban renewal and demolition project after all, and delaying too long will only create more trouble for the Bureau, right?
She crafts her words with meticulous care, gently probing your position. Despite her intentionally courteous manner, you remain unmoved.
After multiple rounds of exchange, you are growing increasingly convinced that Luminita is not as cooperative in this interrogation as she appears to be.
Luminita, you can stop probing my position. I know you want to leave the Bureau, but I'll be perfectly clear with you: given our investigation's findings, that's not going to happen easily.

You've been hiding critical information while only sharing trivial details. So let's start with this: Those properties you handled—were they already "haunted houses" to begin with, or did they only become "haunted" after they fell into your hands?

According to the investigations on the completed property transaction, every "haunted property" handled by Luminita shows evidence of meticulously removed Mania residue. Based on the nature of this Mania, Corruptors may have been present at these sites for extended periods.
Furthermore, testimonies from several of Luminita's fellow agents have indirectly confirmed the suspicion.
"Only Luminita can find, handle, and sell those properties successfully." Your fellow agents speak highly of your skills, but many of them share the Bureau's skepticism about your methods.

Based on evidence gathered from these properties, you're now under serious suspicion of sheltering Corruptors. We suspect that you intentionally used them to fabricate haunted houses and fraudulently profited from the scheme.
Luminita, do you have anything to say in your defense?

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: ...Whoa, you just got real serious all of a sudden. I was expecting you to say something actually important.
After a brief silence, Luminita shrugs her shoulders and spreads her hands with complete indifference, as if the accusations mean nothing to her.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Alright, you got me. I checked all the boxes. But what's that really proving?

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: That I'm a genius at using Corruptors to fake supernatural activities and market "haunted" houses? That I was born for real estate? Look, what I did didn't hurt anyone or cause any real damage.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: If my little tricks qualify as "fraud," then half the Eastside real estate agencies belong behind bars. Would certainly save you the trouble of running around collecting statements from those agents in town.
Setting aside the consequences of what you call "little tricks," simply gathering Corruptors already constitutes a serious prohibited offense.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: This sort of... minor violation should be nothing new for the MBCC Chief... Hey, don't look at me like that. I'm just joking.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Look, I know I've broken some rules, and that's why I've been cooperating with your investigation. But let's be clear: even with my record, that has nothing to do with the developer's property inspection request.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: I've never even been to that old district. Not once!
If you've never been there, how could you be so certain that the "hauntings" were caused by aging facilities rather than Corruptors?
A tense silence suddenly envelops the interrogation room, your words lingering in the air. Luminita narrows her eyes, scrutinizing you closely, the once casual smile on her face fading away.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: I was just talking off the cuff. No need to get hung up on word choice... So what you're implying, Chief, is that you suspect I'm behind the haunting rumors in the old district?
I'm just pointing out a possibility. After all, our investigation shows that staging fake hauntings has been your standard practice in your haunted property dealings.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: That was for profit before—to sell houses. But what would I gain from doing it this time? Sabotage the demolition so I never receive my final payment from the client? Does that make any sense?

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: You're giving me way too much credit, Chief. Is overthinking everything just a professional habit in law enforcement?
Maybe. A lot of times I wish I was just overthinking things.
Currently, we have no evidence linking you to the hauntings in the old district, but at the same time, we can't entirely clear you of suspicion.
The investigation into your past activities remains incomplete. To mitigate potential risks, the Bureau will need to maintain certain restrictions on you...

You purposefully pause. Luminita's expression stays composed, showing no immediate reaction to your words, but the subtle tightening of her posture betrays her underlying nervousness, allowing you to catch a crack in her facade.
Don't think this deal will be your ticket out of the Bureau, Luminita.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: So... what are you going to do about the developer's request?

Since you yourself raised the possibility of Corruptors causing these paranormal events, our top priority before demolition begins will be detecting and eliminating any Mania influence. This is exactly the kind of situation the Bureau specializes in handling.
If the scans detect any anomalies, the demolition will be halted and postponed. And given your history of using Corruptors to fake hauntings, you can expect a much deeper investigation.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: And if there are no issues?
We still have other options to handle it without requiring your involvement.
You deliberately maintain a stern tone while carefully observing Luminita's reaction. Her expression visibly stiffens with each word.

Just when you expect her mood to deteriorate further and reveal her true motives for pursuing this request, she suddenly bursts into laughter, reverting to that same carefree, joking demeanor she displayed at the beginning of the interrogation.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: You're right—you definitely should scan the area first. That old district's so isolated, Corruptors could've easily wandered in. Seen it happen plenty of times before.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Still, I'd recommend letting me check the property myself after you've finished your part.
Luminita's abrupt shift in attitude momentarily catches you off guard.
Why do you have to go there?

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: It's not like I absolutely have to go. Besides, weren't you the one who brought up this request thing, Chief? I know the Bureau doesn't just let Sinners walk around, but...

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Special cases require special treatment, you know? I signed the property inspection agreement, so if I don't show up to finalize it, the developer could claim breach of contract and bleed the Bureau dry.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Just look at this penalty clause—it's multiple times the commission! I wouldn't just lose the money; I'd be paying out of pocket. That would ruin my name in the business!

She reopens the property inspection agreement that was set aside, her finger repeatedly circling the violation penalties on the last page—a pointed reminder of her shrewd, profit-driven nature as an agent.
Luminita's reasoning sounds plausible enough, but this vague, one-size-fits-all explanation might just be her way of talking in circles to shut down further questions.
As you ponder the details of Luminita's behavior during the interrogation, something feels off. A question that's been bothering you since the beginning comes creeping back.
If you're only in real estate for the money, why go through the trouble of faking haunted houses? Normal properties would be much easier to sell.
Someone with your talents doesn't need cheap haunted house stunts.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Not really, Chief. Every industry's its own world with layers you wouldn't see. You've never been in real estate; you don't know how things actually work.
Sure enough, she brushes you off again.

Meeting your gaze, Luminita smiles slightly, almost as if she can read your thoughts. In the tense silence between you, it dawns upon you that this interrogation has hit a wall—you lack the evidence needed to challenge her claims.
You need an opening to make her slip up and reveal her true intentions.
You produce the document you have prepared in advance. When Luminita reads its contents, a flicker of suspicion crosses her face, only to be quickly masked by the same nonchalant smile.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: ...Wait, what? So this whole time, you were just trying to scare me?

Think of it as standard procedure. But you're right about one thing—the Bureau is getting tired of the real estate developer's constant pressure. Sending you in would be the quickest way to resolve the situation.
However, in exchange, I'll be accompanying you the entire time.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: So, Chief... you sure you're not in the market for a house?

On the way back to the detention area, Luminita hastens her steps to move ahead of you. While walking backward to maintain eye contact, she seamlessly transitions back into her salesperson persona, dispelling the serious atmosphere of the interrogation room within seconds.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: The old district inspection will only take half a day at most. How about I show you some properties with the rest of our time? Even if you're not buying, it doesn't hurt to look, right?
...You really don't need to focus so much on me as a potential client.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: It's not just about selling to you! I treat all clients without homes equally—that's my core principle as an agent!
Fortunately, the path isn't long, and Luminita's unyielding sales pitch, which allows you no breathing space, finally comes to a halt as you reach a fork in the corridor.

After saying goodbye, she hurries away with quick, long strides. You watch her figure disappear and begin to breathe a sigh of relief when you suddenly notice something odd—your pocket feels unusually bulky.
You reach into your pocket and a thick stack of business cards comes tumbling out all at once, scattering across the ground.
